One loop. Several ways in.

Start from source material, a rough idea, a ready intent, an existing codebase, or a change you can describe in one sentence. BMad’s skills help you settle the decisions, implement the work, and learn from what actually happened.

What are you bringing?

One clear change goes straight to Build

A testable outcome that fits one implementation session can start from a sentence, issue, specification, or ticket.

Mermaid flowchart
Mermaid source
  1. Start a fresh chat and invoke bmad-build with the change.
  2. Build inspects the repo and settles the design. Review a written plan when a consequential gap, irreversible action, or larger footprint calls for it.
  3. Review the result and decide whether it is done.

What you get One reviewed change, verification evidence, a plan, and a local commit in the documented Git workflow.

Work with the rules your team already has

Set shared defaults in _bmad/custom/<skill>.toml and personal overrides in <skill>.user.toml. bmad-customize writes and verifies per-skill overrides. Central config and document templates have their own surfaces.

What gets passed forward

Each planning skill supplies a missing decision or piece of evidence. Pick the skills the work calls for. A defined intent gives the next person enough to identify the desired outcome, what must stay true, and what falls outside the work.

NeedSkill or roleHandoff
Turn raw material into usable contextbmad-ingestA Markdown note that links to the original and cites sections, pages, quotes, messages, or timestamps. A brief, PRD, architecture, or ticket can link the note.
Generate options or challenge an ideabmad-brainstorming or bmad-forge-ideaBrainstorm notes or a hardened intent. Forge can also recommend dropping the idea.
Evidence to make a decisionbmad-deep-reconCited research summary. Draft a search prompt, process an existing report, or run research in the session.
Capture or test the product conceptMary · bmad-agent-analystProduct brief for a clear concept, PRFAQ to test customer value, or a BRD for a formal business baseline when called for.
Agree on the product across people or epicsJohn · bmad-agent-pmPRD or another planning document. Use validation for findings before sign-off.
Keep UX and technical decisions consistentSally · bmad-ux
Winston · bmad-architecture		DESIGN.md, EXPERIENCE.md, or an architecture spine with shared technical decisions.
Turn the intent into buildable unitsSofia · bmad-agent-poTicket Requirements and Constraints, traceable R<n> IDs, and ordered entries with requirement coverage and dependencies.

The planning tree for larger work

  1. InitiativeShared product intent and constraints. Holds the epic breakdown.
  2. EpicOne coherent outcome. Refine it before planning its stories.
  3. Story or bug entryBuild order, dependency and requirement coverage in tickets/tickets.toml.
  4. One Build sessionAcceptance criteria, reviewed code, and a plan joined to that entry.

An epic can start at the second box. A standalone bug can use backlog/ or go straight to Build. A story entry can be built without creating a leaf file when refinement is unnecessary.

Inside one Build session

bmad-build investigates the request and the repository before asking questions. It chooses a route based on material intent gaps, irreversible actions, and the change’s footprint.

  1. Resolve intentRead the code, the request, and relevant upstream decisions.
  2. Size the planA simple settled design can take the light path. A flagged design gets a written plan and owner approval.
  3. Implement and verifyChange one unit, run relevant checks, and use independent review and triage by default.
  4. Save builtRecord the plan and result. The owner or orchestrator decides when the ticket is done.

Interactive Build

Use it for consequential or foundational decisions, and to settle a plan with the person who owns the change. If review exposes an upstream problem, correct the design or intent and rerun the affected work.

Build a Change · Walk Through a Change

Build Auto

bmad-build-auto takes one explicitly named intent or ticket and returns a terminal result. It can halt blocked. A human or orchestrator selects subsequent work and honors ticket checkpoints.

Autonomous Development Loops

Build and review settings

Build and Build Auto use the renderer and skill-local defaults plus overrides. workflow.route supports auto, oneshot, and full. Both default to quick review. The ordinary invocation can request a different route or none, quick, or thorough review. bmad-code-review is available for a standalone review and defaults to thorough.

Teams can customize implementation handoffs and review lenses, including dispatching a reviewer through a different model where supported. Configuration lives in the workflow overrides and in the tool that runs the workflow.

Build entrypoint · Build defaults · Review a Change

How evidence changes the plan

Ticket review checks an individual change. The retrospective checks how all the changes behave together and whether the epic met its own criteria.

  1. Collect the evidenceRead the epic criteria, ticket plans, commits, and diff. Exercise the changed behavior.
  2. Judge the epicbmad-retrospective records accepted, accepted-with-open-items, or rejected.
  3. Decide what to carryThe owner decides which fixes, decision records, or reconciliations to accept.
  4. Update upstreamAsk Sofia to replan from changed requirements or dependencies and keep stable IDs for impact tracking.
Where an organization can attach sign-off
Decision momentWork it gates

Align these points with existing approvals. Route a requested change back to its source document before re-running downstream skills.

What the index is doing

The home page is a decision surface for people arriving with different levels of certainty. The linked guides show how its short loop turns into concrete work. The observations below read the index alongside those guides and this checkout’s skill definitions.

Intent determines the entry point

The diagram places vague input at Clarify, clear large work at Plan, and a small change at Build. The planning guide makes the distinction testable: can someone use the stated outcome, constraints, and boundaries without guessing? Build can investigate a rough request before concluding that it needs another planning step.

Index · Find Your Starting Point · Planning Path · Build a Change

Scale changes coordination

The same implementation unit recurs at every scale. An epic adds a coherent outcome, a story sequence, and a combined verdict. A project adds shared product and architectural decisions plus boundaries for parallel work. Size estimates are signals alongside risk, uncertainty, and cross-team dependencies.

Planning Path · UX and Architecture

Artifacts carry the decisions

Bring a pile of source material through Ingest so the next skill can work from a short note and trace its claims back to the original. Thinking skills can end at a brief or research report. For ticketed work, Sofia turns the relevant inputs into requirements with stable IDs. Build reads those requirements and the pertinent references. Plans preserve what was verified for later work.

Index · Thinking and Building · Ingest · Requirements and Specification · Stories and Tracking

Completion includes an owner decision

The index’s promise that you make the calls shows up at plan approvals, built to done, and epic acceptance. Unattended execution shrinks the interaction inside one unit. Dispatch, prioritization, and acceptance still belong to the human or orchestrator.

Index · Hero · Autonomous Development Loops · Finish an Epic

The index compresses two thresholds into one picture. The linked guides clarify both: a trivial edit may bypass BMad entirely, and clear large work still needs a breakdown before implementation. Existing codebases and team conventions affect the context of either path.
